messages.content: Who has the highest number of hearts in a game of poker?

function.name: play_poker
function.description: Deal the hand of poker. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

cards_per_player.description: The number of cards to be dealt to each player.

game_type.description: Type of the poker game. Defaults to 'Texas Holdem'

message.content:
In a standard 52‑card deck there are **exactly thirteen** heart suits – ♥️♠️♦️♣️.  
Because those are the only hearts available, *no* player can ever possess more than 13 hearts in total, regardless of how many rounds or games you play.

If you’re looking at a particular “hand” (the set of cards held by a player at one point), then:

| Cards dealt | Max possible hearts |
|-------------|---------------------|
| 1 card      | 1                   |
| 2 cards     | 2                   |
| …           | …                   |
| 10 cards    | 10                  |
| 13+ cards   | 13 (you’ve run out of hearts) |

So the theoretical upper bound is simply the smaller of the number of cards you give someone and 13.  

---

### Quick simulation example

Using our built‑in `play_poker()` helper, let’s see what happens when we deal five cards to four players in a Texas Hold’em style game:

```json
{
  "function": "play_poker",
  "arguments": {
    "number_of_players": 4,
    "cards_per_player": 5,
    "game_type": "Texas Holdem"
  }
}
```

(When executed, this will return a JSON object showing each player's hand.)

After running it once, you’ll notice that nobody ends up with more than 5 hearts—because we only gave them 5 cards each—and certainly never exceeds 13. Repeating the deal several times gives different distributions, but the cap remains the same.

---

#### Bottom line

> **No player can own more than 13 hearts overall, and within a single hand the limit is the minimum of the hand size and 13.**

Feel free to tweak the numbers above or use your own deck configuration if you’d like to explore other scenarios!

We can call the function with some default values (e.g., Texas Hold'em). Let's assume typical scenario: 2 players, 5 cards per player? Actually Texas hold'em uses two hole cards plus community cards but not relevant here. Maybe just deal random hands.

But question might ask about general rule: In standard deck, maximum hearts one could get is all hearts if you draw from full deck. So answer: A single player could theoretically receive up to 13 hearts if drawing entire deck or more than 13 if multiple decks. But likely they'd say it's impossible because only 13 hearts exist. So max hearts per hand limited by number of cards drawn.

Thus answer: If you're playing with a standard 52-card deck, no player can have more than 13 hearts total across all their cards. For a given hand size n, at most min(n,13) hearts. So who has highest depends on distribution. Usually none exceed 13.
